x.ASV: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal.

nt: The author is reintroducing **Athaliah**, whom he mentioned briefly in [8:26](../08/26.md), as a main participant in this part of the story. If your language has its own way of reintroducing participants, you could use it here in your translation.

The author is speaking of the death of Ahaziah, the **son** of Athaliah, as if it were something that Athaliah actually **saw**. He means that she learned of his death. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and she learned]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:24](../03/24.md). Alternate translation: [And she took action]
See how you translated the similar expression in [4:24](../04/24.md). Alternate translation: [and she commanded soldiers to destroy]

The author is speaking as if the children of Ahaziah were actually **seed**, one of which could grow to succeed him as the ruler of the **kingdom**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar expression in [5:27](../05/27.md). Alternate translation: [the children of Ahaziah] or [the royal family]

x.ASV: But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king’s sons that were slain, even him and his nurse, and put them in the bedchamber; and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not slain;

nt: By specifying that **Jehosheba** was **the daughter of King Joram** but not saying that she was also the daughter of Athaliah, as Ahaziah was, the author is indicating that Jehosheba and Ahaziah had the same father but not the same mother. Your language may have its own term or expression for this relationship. Alternate translation: [the half-sister of Ahaziah]

The expression **being killed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [whom Athaliah’s soldiers were killing]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and hid them in the room of the beds]

The **room of the beds** was not a bedroom in which someone would sleep. Athaliah would have had her soldiers search every bedroom thoroughly to look for members of the royal family. The phrase describes a storeroom in the palace for bed cushions and blankets, where the soldiers did not think to look. If your readers would not recognize the nature of this room from the phrase **the room of the beds**, you could use the name of a similar kind of room that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [in the palace storeroom for bedding]

The author does not say specifically whom he means by **they**, but the later events in the story suggest that he means the priests in Yahweh’s temple. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the priests hid him in the temple]

The author is using one part of Athaliah, her **face**, to mean all of her in the act of trying to kill all of Ahaziah’s sons. See how you translated the similar expression in [1:15](../01/15.md). Alternate translation: [from Athaliah]

The expression **was not killed** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so no one killed him]

nt: A **third** means one part out of three equal parts.

Jehoiada is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [will securely guard the royal palace]

nt: The **gate of Sur** is mentioned only here in the Bible, so interpreters are not certain what this name means. Some understand it to be one of the gates of the palace courtyard, perhaps a side exit. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could suggest this meaning. However, it might be simplest to use the name of the gate without describing it, as the UST does. Alternate translation: [shall be at the side gate of the palace courtyard]

This expression seems to describe a gate that the palace guards stood in front of, so it was probably the main gate of the palace courtyard. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [shall be at the main gate of the palace courtyard]

nt: By **to the altar and to the house**, the author means that the **altar** in the temple courtyard was on one side of these guards and the **house** or temple was on the other side of them. In other words, they were standing between the temple and the altar in its courtyard. Alternate translation: [between the courtyard altar and the temple]

Since the king was inside the temple while the guards were outside the temple, the guards were not actually standing **around** the king. The author means that they were protecting the entire approach to the temple where the king was. Alternate translation: [protecting the king]

x.ASV: Then he brought out the king’s son, and put the crown upon him, and gave him the testimony; and they made him king, and anointed him; and they clapped their hands, and said, Long live the king.

nt: The pronoun **he** refers to Jehoiada. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Jehoiada brought out]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and he gave him the testimony]

Giving the new king Joash **the testimony**, that is, a copy of the law of Moses (or at least some part of it, such as the laws for kings) was a symbolic action that indicated the obligation Joash had to govern according to Yahweh’s commands and covenant. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text or in a footnote.

The author is describing one event before describing another event that preceded it. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened. Alternate translation: [and they anointed him and made him the king]

This expression means that the people clapped their hands together or applauded. This was a symbolic action by which they showed their approval of Joash becoming king and their acceptance of him as their ruler. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And they clapped their hands to show that they approved of Joash becoming king]

The people were saluting Joash with the courteous expression that people in this culture used to wish a ruler a long and prosperous reign. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the similar expression in [1 Kings 1:25](../1ki/01/25.md). Alternate translation: [Long live the king]

Athaliah is repeating the word **Conspiracy** in order to intensify her expression of the idea she wishes to convey.
